sourcedFrom: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) (cached from a 2025 capture)
cleanIntro: A direct-impingement AR, and Rock River's own book is more specific than most on two points. ⛔ THE TAKEDOWN AND PIVOT PINS GO TO THE SECOND DETENT AND NO FURTHER — Rock River says pushing either one past it causes IRREPARABLE damage to the lower receiver, and that a punch is never used to drive them. ⛔ AND IT PUBLISHES THE EXTRACTOR TEST: push the back of the extractor; if it does not spring back, it comes out and gets cleaned. That is the check most AR owners never make.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE — and it needs a cocked hammer
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger. Put the safety selector on SAFE. If it will not go, the hammer is not cocked — cycle the charging handle first rather than forcing the lever.
steps.prose: Rock River prints that note beside the step because the interlock surprises people every time they strip a rifle after dry-firing it.
steps.aside: Note: If hammer is not cocked, safety selector can not be placed on SAFE.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Inspect For Ammunition, printed pp.11-12

steps.title: Bolt locked open, THEN the magazine out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle rearward; while holding the bolt back, engage the bolt catch by pushing in on its lower portion and ease the charging handle forward until the catch locks the bolt open. Then press the magazine catch button and remove the magazine.
steps.prose: Note the order Rock River gives — bolt open first, magazine second. On a rifle already locked open there is nothing left to feed, so the chamber cannot refill while your hands are busy.
steps.quote: Pull charging handle (B) rearward. While retaining bolt in rearward position, engage bolt catch by pushing inward on its lower portion (C) and slowly releasing charging handle until bolt catch engages bolt and locks it open.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Inspect For Ammunition, printed pp.11-12

steps.title: Look into the receiver, and do it EVERY time
steps.action: Look into the receiver and verify there is no ammunition in the chamber. Then, with the selector still pointing toward SAFE, let the bolt go forward by pressing the top of the bolt catch.
steps.prose: Rock River lists exactly when this inspection is owed: before cleaning, before storage, before transport, before handing the rifle to anyone and when one is handed to you.
steps.quote: Follow this inspection procedure before cleaning, before storage, before transporting, before handing to another person or when handed to you.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Inspect For Ammunition, printed pp.11-12

steps.title: ⛔ Takedown pin to the SECOND DETENT — not past it
steps.action: With the selector on SAFE and the bolt forward, push the takedown pin to the second detent position. If it is tight, use the chamber flag as a pusher. ⛔ Never use a punch to drive the pin.
steps.prose: ⛔ Rock River's warning is unusually blunt and worth obeying literally: past the second detent and the damage to the lower receiver is IRREPARABLE. Closed is the first position; the second is where it stops.
steps.quote: Pushing takedown pin past the second detent position (with closed being the first position) A will result in irreparable damage to the lower receiver.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembly, printed pp.23-26
steps.warn: Do not disassemble firearm any further than instructed in this manual. Do not modify or alter firearm. Never interchange parts from other firearms.

steps.title: Pivot pin the same way, then split the receivers
steps.action: Push the pivot pin to its second detent, again with the chamber flag rather than a punch, and separate the upper receiver from the lower.
steps.prose: Same rule, same consequence. Both pins are captive and both have exactly one correct stopping point.
steps.quote: Pushing pivot pin past the second detent position (with closed being the first position) will result in irreparable damage to the lower receiver.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembly, printed pp.23-26

steps.title: Charging handle and bolt carrier out together
steps.action: Pull rearward on the charging handle to draw the charging handle and bolt carrier out of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: They come out as a pair on this rifle's own instruction — the carrier rides the handle until the handle reaches its keyway.
steps.quote: Pull rearward on charging handle (C) to remove charging handle and bolt carrier.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembly, printed pp.23-26

steps.title: ⛔ Bore from the BREECH, and take the tip off first
steps.action: Clean the barrel with the upper separated from the lower. Solvent on a cotton patch, rod in at the chamber and out at the muzzle, repeating with clean patches until one stays clean. A bronze bore brush to loosen what the patches will not.
steps.prose: ⛔ Rock River adds a detail almost nobody follows: take the patch, brush or jag OFF the rod before pulling the rod back through the bore. A single-piece coated rod, and nothing that can score the bore.
steps.quote: RRA also recommends cleaning from the breech (chamber) to the muzzle and removal of the patch, brush, jag, or other cleaning device from the rod prior to pulling the rod back through the bore.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning, printed pp.27-30

steps.title: Chamber and the barrel LOCKING LUGS
steps.action: Solvent and a chamber brush through the chamber and the barrel locking lugs, several passes, then clean patches until one stays clean. Light oil after — and take it back out before shooting.
steps.prose: The lug recesses are where carbon actually collects on an AR and where it eventually stops the bolt turning into battery. A chamber brush reaches them; a bore brush does not.
steps.aside: Once clean, apply a light coating of oil to the chamber (remove prior to shooting).
steps.quote: Clean the chamber and barrel locking lugs with solvent and a chamber cleaning brush. Move the brush through the chamber several times to scrub the inside of the chamber.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning, printed pp.27-30

steps.title: ⛔ Never grease the trigger mechanism
steps.action: Wipe every metal surface of the lower with a clean cloth and follow with a lightly oiled one. Wipe debris out of the trigger mechanism. Compressed air helps here — with eye protection on.
steps.prose: ⛔ Grease in an AR trigger group is a specific prohibition in this book, and the reason is that grease holds the grit that a light oil lets go.
steps.quote: Never apply grease to trigger mechanism.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning, printed pp.27-30

steps.title: Upper receiver and the bolt carrier channel
steps.action: Wipe the upper inside and out with a clean cloth then a lightly oiled one, and clear debris from the bolt carrier channel.
steps.prose: The channel is the surface the carrier actually rides on. Carbon there is what turns a smooth rifle gritty long before it causes a stoppage.
steps.quote: Wipe any debris from the bolt carrier channel.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning, printed pp.27-30

steps.title: ⛔ Light oil, never heavy oil or grease
steps.action: Lightly lubricate with a cleaner/lubricant/preservative: the inside of the upper, bore and chamber; the outer barrel; all moving lower parts with their pins and detents, including the takedown and pivot pins; the firing pin and its recess; the carrier inside and out; the bolt, cam pin and gas rings; the extractor and its pin. ⛔ Dry the inside of the carrier key with a cotton swab and put ONE drop in.
steps.prose: ⛔ Rock River repeats "never use a heavy oil or grease" on each of the three lubrication lists. And it asks for fingerprints to be wiped off with the same product — finger moisture starts corrosion.
steps.quote: The inside of the carrier key on the bolt carrier should be dried with a cotton swab, then place one drop of Cleaner/Lubricant/Preservative inside.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Lubrication, printed p.31

steps.title: Field strip complete — the deep clean is the bolt
steps.action: Upper, lower, bolt carrier group and charging handle. Rock River does publish the bolt-group strip and the extractor, and that is the DEEP CLEAN below.
steps.prose: ⛔ Past the bolt group there is nothing published for an owner, and Rock River asks you to phone rather than improvise if a part will not come out.
steps.quote: Do not disassemble firearm any further than instructed in this manual.
steps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembly, printed pp.23-26

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin — do not distort the ends
deepSteps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin out of the carrier, taking care not to bend or flatten its ends.
deepSteps.prose: It is a spring-steel cotter pin and its ends are what keep it captive. Rock River separately forbids substituting an ordinary cotter pin for it — the round head shape damages the carrier.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin retaining pin (A). Do not distort the ends of the retaining pin.
deepSteps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembly, printed pp.23-26

deepSteps.title: Bolt IN, then the firing pin out the back
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt assembly into the carrier to its locked position, then take the firing pin out through the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Bolt in first, every time — the firing pin cannot clear until the bolt is pushed home.
deepSteps.quote: Insert the firing pin (F) through the rear of the bolt carrier assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Assembly, printed pp.32-34

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Cam pin 90 degrees — and if it will not come out, PHONE
deepSteps.action: Rotate the bolt cam pin 90 degrees and lift it out of the carrier, then withdraw the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Rock River's instruction for a cam pin that will not come out is to contact them, not to lever at it. A bent cam pin is a rifle that short-strokes and a broken one is a rifle that will not fire.
deepSteps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembly, printed pp.23-26

deepSteps.title: ⛔ THE EXTRACTOR TEST most owners never do
deepSteps.action: Push in on the rear of the extractor. If it springs back, leave it. If it does NOT spring back, push the extractor pin out and take the extractor off the bolt for cleaning. ⛔ Do not take the spring insert out of the extractor spring.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ This is the single most useful check in the book. A sluggish extractor is carbon under the spring, and the symptom is failures to extract that look like an ammunition problem. The insert is a separate part that must stay in the spring.
deepSteps.aside: Do not remove extractor spring insert from extractor spring (G).
deepSteps.quote: Push in on the rear of the extractor (E). If the extractor does not spring back, remove the extractor from the bolt (D) for cleaning.
deepSteps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembly, printed pp.23-26

deepSteps.title: Carbon off the bolt and carrier, then INSPECT
deepSteps.action: Wipe every bolt carrier group surface and follow with a lightly oiled cloth. Scrape the carbon build-up off both the bolt and the carrier, and wipe the firing pin, retaining pin, cam pin and extractor.
deepSteps.prose: A dedicated bolt scraper is the right tool here; the tail of the bolt carries a hard carbon ring that a cloth will not shift.
deepSteps.quote: Clean any carbon fouling/buildup from both the bolt and carrier using the CAT M4 Bolt Tool (RRA Part AR3550) or similar product.
deepSteps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning, printed pp.27-30

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The six checks that decide whether a part goes back in
deepSteps.action: Bolt: cracks or fractures, especially around the cam pin hole; pitting into the firing pin hole means replace. Firing pin: bent, cracked, too blunt, too sharp, or pitted tip means replace — and it must move freely in the bolt. Retaining pin: bent or badly worn means replace. Cam pin: cracked, worn or chipped means replace. Extractor: chipped or broken edges on the lip that grips the case rim means replace.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The cam pin hole is the one to look at hardest — it is where an AR bolt cracks, and a cracked bolt does not warn you first.
deepSteps.aside: Never use a cotter pin as a substitute for a firing pin retaining pin. Cotter pins are not made of heat treated spring steel and their round head shape will cause damage.
deepSteps.quote: Check the bolt for cracks or fractures, especially in the cam pin hole area. Bolts with any pitting extending into the firing pin hole must be replaced.
deepSteps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning, printed pp.27-30

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Rebuild: extractor pin flush, gas rings 120° apart
deepSteps.action: Extractor with its insert and spring back into the bolt, then the extractor pin — which must NOT stand proud on either side. Set the three gas ring gaps 120 degrees apart around the bolt. Bolt into the carrier, cam pin in and rotated 90 degrees so its hole lines up through the bolt, firing pin in from the rear, bolt fully forward, retaining pin in.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Staggering the gas rings is not folklore here — it is Rock River's own reassembly step. And a proud extractor pin drags in the carrier bore.
deepSteps.quote: Extractor pin must not extend outside the bolt on either side.
deepSteps.cite: Rock River Arms LAR-15 Rifles and Pistols Operating & Safety Instruction Manual — LAR-15 Owners Manual (no form code printed) — Assembly, printed pp.32-34

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: ⛔ Breech to muzzle, upper separated from lower
⛔ Take the patch/brush/jag OFF the rod before pulling it back
Chamber brush through the chamber AND the barrel locking lugs

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Scrape carbon off the bolt tail and inside the carrier
⛔ Carrier key DRIED with a swab, then ONE drop of CLP
Gas rings, cam pin, firing pin and extractor wiped

cleaning.name: UPPER RECEIVER
tasks: Interior and exterior wiped, then a lightly oiled cloth
Bolt carrier channel cleared of debris
Light oil in and around the locking lugs

cleaning.name: LOWER RECEIVER
tasks: Compressed air with eye protection on
Light oil on every moving part, pin and detent

reassembly: Extractor, insert and spring into the bolt; extractor pin flush on both sides.
Three gas ring gaps set 120 degrees apart.
Bolt into the carrier, cam pin in and rotated 90 degrees until its hole aligns through the bolt.
Firing pin in through the rear, bolt extended fully forward, retaining pin in.
Carrier and charging handle into the upper, close the receivers and seat both pins.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber verified empty by eye, muzzle safe. Cycle the charging handle and confirm the bolt returns fully into battery. Selector to SAFE and pull the trigger — the hammer must not fall. Selector to FIRE and pull — it should. Then check both takedown pins are fully closed and flush. ⛔ Before that, confirm the cam pin is installed: a rifle fired without it can come apart.
